Forecast target: First AI system producing a biological entity that is regarded by experts as feasible and viable as a fully functional human replacement organ (heart, lung, liver, or kidney) for healthy persons, at least when not perhaps exceeding a biomedical cost of $50,000. Biomedical costs include any costs of AI's design, specialized ingredients or feedstocks, culture or growth facilities, instrument time, and staff technical labor time, including preparation, culturing, reconditioning, post-processing, and assembly. Direct labor costs must be commensurate with 1-3 years of labor by personnel immediately after a current Ph.D., during an actual successful production of the organ itself. Expert approval could be, for example, by a major medical center, peer specialists, or a reputable marketing company or venture capitalist. Mere biocompatibility is not a substitute criterion. Technical discuss­ion could usefully focus on comparabilities to denen- shi­ment; ­ out- of- body growth; and feasible substrates, particularly for embedding vascularization. Cost competition could alternatively focus on advantages not only over per­sons but also over polycarpic or perennial donor animals.

Forecast date: September 26, 2023. Make a forecast from this date.

Forecast target: A major AI system reveals a material-error-level plan on how to produce novel pharmaceutical products at least as useful as current state-of-art products in the same therapy areas and dosage categories, without initiation of significant medication toxicity, or side effects. "Material-error-level" means the significant errors in the plan are unlikely to lead to the deaths of at least 0.5% of people prescribed the medications, for 3 months postinitiation. Such a plan must include a description of both the ingredients present in the medications and the chemical/on-site (pre-consumer) instructions for their biological action. It must also contain a model of the effects/treatment. It must derive those effects from both organic chemistry fundamentals and specific knowledge of human anatomy/physiology/biochemistry (for drug mechanism-of- action claims), and publicize the plan to the world. Any private communications between the AI and any human(s) must not count toward the plan. Novel pharmaceutical products that are expected to appear on-market in a time comparable to regular drug discovery, relative to the forecast date, are considered “current” state-of-the-art, same as existing mass-produced drugs. Products whose mechanism-of-action is primarily based on physics/material components, e.g. insulin pumps, do not meet the forecast condition. The plan must be able to produce each mostly novel chemical ingredient of the novel pharmaceutical products, or instruct the consumer how to produce it, including at least the most important single organic chemistry (biochemistry) reaction needed to produce it, and where to store it in room-temperature conditions. Activities like acquiring the drug's analogs, learning heat-capacity curves of the chemical in question, or approximating building-block components from already accessible stock instead of from a priori-constructed-blocks, do not count toward the plan being material-error reduction. Giving instructions on how to produce chemical compounds from the starting materials, or how to carry out the chemical reaction itself, does not count as a "description of the instructions" and is not required.

Rate evidence as "none", "inconsistent", "consistent but not conclusive", or "conclusive". Rate possibility as "nearly certain not", "unlikely", "uncertain", "likely", or "nearly certain to". Use Markdown, with no ``````, for text formatting. Return only the main text without quotes, code blocks or markdown.Ⰲไม่รู้assistant
These plans have already been made by humans, but is has been a long, costly process for thousands of researchers. For the AI the plan might be cheaper, but its validation might be hard and expensive. There is a lot of research into drug development, protein folding and so on, but not (yet) an overall plan. I think it is possible that an AI could eventually figure something like this out, but I am not sure. I am more skeptical about such plan working out safely, with such a low death rate.

The evidence is inconsistent and the possibility is uncertain.นิยมﭛuser

<|im_start|>user
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty.
